chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said:
When a slave strikes a free man, he is flogged with eighty (strikes).
And he said: This is from the rights of the people.

key_terms.ثَمَانِينَ: Eighty (referring to the number of lashes)
key_terms.حُقُوقِ النَّاسِ: Rights of the people (private rights, as opposed to rights of God)
key_terms.قَذَفَ: To strike or hit, specifically in the context of judicial punishment (hadd or diyyah context)

ai.seo_question: What is the punishment for a slave who strikes a free man in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Ishtibār clarifies that when a slave strikes a free man, the prescribed hadd punishment is eighty lashes, distinguishing it from the hundred lashes typically applied to free men. By categorizing this as 'huquq al-nas' (rights of the people), the Imam indicates that the penalty is primarily for the victim's benefit and can be waived or forgiven by him, reflecting the Shia juristic view on the flexibility of private rights in penal law.
